uses.source_location: Published pp183–185, especially purpose-of-work discussion p185; Sections3–5.
uses.support_explanation: The paper develops Turing-category structure and its PCA correspondence. The manuscript makes only a historical attribution.

uses.source_location: Section2.3.3, published pp241–242; Total(X) definition in Section2.1.2.
uses.support_explanation: The restriction splitting is Kr; its totality criterion gives bar(f)=e.
Stable monic systems give span partial maps, pullback composition, and canonical split restriction.

uses.source_location: Published introduction pp224–225, especially p225; Section2.
uses.support_explanation: The authors introduce restriction categories by taking domain idempotents as primitive.
The four axioms, common-source qualifications, and composition convention agree.

uses.source_location: Section2.3.3, published pp241–242; definition of Kr(X) p242.
uses.support_explanation: The splitting construction, identities, morphism condition, and restriction-idempotent case agree.
Arbitrary idempotents E are allowed; the restriction is bar(f)e as stated.

uses.source_location: Proposition4.5; author arXiv preprint p21, proof pp22–23.
uses.support_explanation: The proposition states exactly the equivalence with binary restriction products.

uses.source_location: Section4.2 and Proposition4.5; author arXiv preprint pp20–23.
uses.support_explanation: The binary-product universal property and equivalence are supported. No terminal object is needed for this equivalence.

uses.source_location: 1995 retypeset author edition: Chapter2 opening p28; Definition2.1.2 p29; Proposition2.2.1 and counterexample p33.
uses.support_explanation: The chapter weakens dominical axioms, proves every dominical category is a p-category, and gives counterexamples to the converse. This supports the historical generalization claim.
uses.required_correction: None. Optional precision: cite Chapter2, especially Proposition2.2.1.

uses.source_location: Author-uploaded chapter fulltext, opening p307, before Section1; retrieved lines918–1071; Definition1.1 and Theorem1.2 p308.
uses.support_explanation: The opening introduces p-categories as a more general algebraic setting than dominical categories; the manuscript makes this historical claim only.
uses.required_correction: None. Optional precision: add p307 to the historical citation.

uses.source_location: Original article fulltext unavailable. Corroborating primary source: Maietti, Definition 2.4 and immediately following paragraph, author PDF p4 (published p42).
uses.support_explanation: Existence and metadata verified. Maietti explicitly corroborates this attribution for lists, but Cockett’s original article was inaccessible. General polynomial initiality is not attributed to this source.
uses.required_correction: No false claim established. Obtain and inspect Cockett's original article to close this use. If it remains unavailable, retain the explicit verification limitation; Maietti alone directly supports the stated list formulation.

uses.source_location: Definition 2.4 and immediately following paragraph, author PDF p4 (0-index P3), published p42; retrieved lines128–160.
uses.support_explanation: Parameterized list recursion is equivalent to preservation of recursive objects by pullback into slices. Regularity supplies finite completeness; the manuscript assumes parameterized initiality separately and limits this attribution to lists.

uses.source_location: Theorem4.7, published pp437–438; Lemma4.12 statement p439, proof p440.
uses.support_explanation: Theorem4.7 gives M-stable factorization through restriction monics. Lemma4.12 connects the earlier agreement-law definition to the range axioms.
uses.required_correction: None required. Optional locator clarification: attach Lemma4.12 to the preceding agreement-law definition and retain Theorem4.7 for factorization.

uses.support_explanation: Regular D supplies stable regular-epi/mono factorization for Theorem4.5. Section4.11 explains the stronger agreement law; no regularity is inferred from split ranges alone.

uses.source_location: Section3.16 p479 and Proposition3.17 p480; compare Theorem3.18 p480.
uses.support_explanation: Finite limits and stable factorization become regular epi/mono precisely when M contains all monics. The manuscript separately assumes regularity.

uses.source_location: Published article pp108–109, example immediately before Proposition2.4; author-uploaded fulltext lines1328–1390.
uses.support_explanation: The PA example uses provably single-valued Sigma1 formulas modulo provable identity. The manuscript cites that presentation and supplies its own construction for general T.

qualification: Metadata verification and textual support are separate. Fulltext-unavailable does not mean invented. The CGHRangeI line649 locator clarification is optional because Theorem4.7 supports the sentence and Lemma4.12 supports the immediately preceding range convention.
